hypotheses.title: Decayed Direct Competitor Lead-Lag Catch-Up Revaluation
hypotheses.economic_rationale: In corporate supply-chain and competitor networks (pv13, Matrix 82% coverage), direct competitors (rel_ret_comp) share identical macroeconomic inputs and customer demands. Competitor price discovery leads individual equity adjustments due to segmented order flow. In Batch 295, this competitor lead-lag spread generated Sharpe 1.53 and Sub-universe Sharpe 1.17 with zero correlation flags, but exhibited high turnover (45.34%) under a 5-day decay window. Lengthening the linear decay horizon to 12 days dampens daily return noise, compressing turnover to ~18-20% to drive Fitness well above 1.00 while preserving zero correlation to fundamental/analyst signals.
confounders: Permanent structural market share losses that justify widening competitor return divergence
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if competitor lead-lag spread yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 12-day decayed spread between direct competitor returns and focal equity dimensionless returns for disciplined turnover compression.

hypotheses.title: Intraday Liquidity Deficit and VWAP Slippage Reversal
hypotheses.economic_rationale: When an equity closes significantly below its volume-weighted average price ((vwap - close) / (high - low + 0.001) > 0) across 100% coverage in TOP3000 (pv1), aggressive market-on-close sellers dumped liquidity at an excessive execution discount. Market makers absorb this inventory and systematically re-rate the depressed equity over the subsequent 6 days as order imbalance clears. This pure microstructure dynamic is orthogonal to relationship and accounting datasets, guaranteeing self-correlation < 0.40.
confounders: Late-day catastrophic news announcements that justify continued structural price collapse
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if VWAP discount reversal yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 6-day linear decay of true-range normalized VWAP execution discount.

hypotheses.title: Rolling Cashflow Efficiency Acceleration Inflection
hypotheses.economic_rationale: cashflow_efficiency_rank_derivative (Matrix 100% coverage in model16) measures the daily rate of change in operational cash generation efficiency per unit of capital. Evaluating when this derivative reaches a 15-day rolling historical peak (ts_rank(cashflow_efficiency_rank_derivative, 15)) isolates rapid fundamental cash turnaround before consensus estimates reflect balance-sheet strength. A 15-day window prevents turnover freezing while maintaining zero correlation to analyst and relationship datasets.
confounders: Temporary working capital timing distortions that artificially inflate short-term cash flow efficiency
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if cashflow efficiency acceleration yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 4-day linear decay of 15-day rolling rank of daily cashflow efficiency derivative.
